sites.name: Willis Tower
sites.fact: Completed in 1973 as the Sears Tower. At 442 metres it was the tallest building in the world for 25 years.
sites.hint: The dark stepped tower with two white antennas, west of the Loop.

sites.name: Cloud Gate
sites.fact: A polished steel sculpture in Millennium Park, nicknamed the Bean. It weighs about 110 tons.
sites.hint: In Millennium Park, between the towers and the lake.

sites.name: Navy Pier
sites.fact: A pier more than 3,000 feet long, opened in 1916. Its Ferris wheel recalls the very first one, built in Chicago for the 1893 World's Fair.
sites.hint: The long pier into the lake, just north of the river mouth.

sites.name: Wrigley Field
sites.fact: Home of the Cubs since 1916 and the second-oldest ballpark in the major leagues. Ivy covers the outfield wall.
sites.hint: A ballpark among houses on the North Side.

sites.name: Soldier Field
sites.fact: Opened in 1924 as a memorial to American soldiers. The Bears have played here since 1971.
sites.hint: The stadium with classical colonnades on the lakefront, south of the Loop.

sites.name: 875 North Michigan Avenue
sites.fact: Completed in 1969 and long known as the John Hancock Center. The X-shaped braces on its outside help hold it up.
sites.hint: The dark tapering tower with crossed braces, north of the river.

sites.name: Lincoln Park Zoo
sites.fact: Founded in 1868 and still free to enter, one of the oldest zoos in North America.
sites.hint: In the long lakefront park north of downtown.

sites.name: Adler Planetarium
sites.fact: The first planetarium in the Western Hemisphere, opened in 1930 at the tip of a peninsula in the lake.
sites.hint: At the end of the spit of land east of Soldier Field.

sites.name: University of Chicago
sites.fact: Founded in 1890. The first controlled nuclear chain reaction took place here in 1942, under the stands of a football field.
sites.hint: Grey stone quadrangles in Hyde Park, on the South Side.

sites.name: Midway Airport
sites.fact: Until O'Hare opened to airlines in 1955, this one square mile was the busiest airport in the world.
sites.hint: A square airfield hemmed in by houses, south-west of the Loop.

sites.name: United Center
sites.fact: Home of the Bulls and the Blackhawks since 1994. A statue of Michael Jordan stands inside.
sites.hint: The big arena west of the Loop.

sites.name: Wolf Point
sites.fact: Where the branches of the Chicago River meet. Engineers reversed the river in 1900 so that it flows away from Lake Michigan, the city's drinking water.
sites.hint: Where the river splits in three, at the north-west corner of the Loop.
